task.description: WF-03 Step 3c hard gate: idiom/quality of InvocationLease, supervision integrity, the AC1->AC4 merge, the AC5 string replay, dispatch count, non-vacuity, a challenge of ORCH's OQ-E resolution (§10), and scope.

result.summary:
PASS, with one MAJOR and three MINOR findings, none of which block merge but the MAJOR must be corrected in the design doc / a future comment pass since it misstates a number this run's own gate (OQ-E) treats as load-bearing.

=== 1. IDIOM AND QUALITY of invocation_lease.ex -- CLEAN ===
Read the file in full. This is an idiomatic GenServer: opaque Lease struct (@enforce_keys, no exposed internals), monitor-backed release keyed to the ACQUIRING pid (elem(from,0)) rather than trusting cooperation -- correctly generalizes SandboxPool's owner_ref = Process.monitor(owner_pid) precedent (verified real, sandbox_pool.ex:567). demonitor+flush on explicit release (verified real precedent, sandbox_pool.ex:407's own flush-so-a-normal-return-never-also-delivers-a-:DOWN pattern) closes the exact race invocation_lease_test.exs's own test (:119-147) targets -- reproduced independently (see section 6 below) that this test genuinely discriminates the race, not merely exercises the code path. handle_info({:DOWN,...}) no-ops on a stale ref not present in `leases` (mirrors pollers_breaker.ex:163-171's real stale-:DOWN precedent, verified). try_acquire evaluates before mutating with no rollback path (matches Admission's own documented discipline, verified against admission.ex:186-258's real max(pool_size - reserved_headroom, 1) floor and Keyword.get_lazy usage). No crutch pattern found -- this is not gen_statem territory (a counting semaphore has no per-state callback shape to fake), and nothing here hand-rolls a state machine via case/cond in place of a real OTP behaviour.

The moduledoc (read in full) carries every clause design doc S7 mandates verbatim in substance: production-does-not-call-this-yet stated with equal prominence to the native-leak non-guarantee, what the module DOES guarantee, and why a new module rather than Admission. A future maintainer who only opens this file, never the design doc, gets the same warning ORCH's own S0 insists on. No finding.

=== 2. SUPERVISION INTEGRITY -- CLEAN, cross-checked against the diff, not the handoff's narrative ===
git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/supervisor/infrastructure.ex confirms: child 11 of 18 (was 17), inserted directly after PluginTaskSupervisor, with init/1 reading only static Application.get_env (no Repo/Registry/other-process dependency) -- the 'no ordering dependency' claim holds on direct inspection of init/1 (:186-190 of invocation_lease.ex: only Map literal construction, no side effects). Every count reference the ISS-0429 bullet touches (moduledoc numbered list, the 'child 17'->'child 18' ordering-guarantee bullet, the inline comment at the Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor child spec, the Task.Supervisor-sprawl-review sentence) was updated consistently -- verified via the actual diff hunks, not the ELIXIR-DEV summary. No stale '17' reference found anywhere in the file. No finding.

=== 3. THE AC1->AC4 MERGE -- VERIFIED PRESENT, all three assertions confirmed in the real file ===
Read plugin_handler_test.exs:518-528 directly (not the handoff's claim about it). AC4's first (300ms) dispatch now asserts, in order: `assert {:error, short_reason} = short_result`, `assert is_binary(short_reason)`, `assert short_elapsed_ms < 10_000` (with the same message text as AC1's own former bound), and `assert CallTimeout.classify(short_result) == :wall_clock_timeout` -- all four checked against that SAME dispatch's own short_result/short_elapsed_ms, no new dispatch added. This matches design S6.2's controlling instruction (not S6.3.1's looser wording, which CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own regate-2 already flagged MINOR for the same ambiguity) exactly. AC1's own test body is confirmed deleted (git diff shows the full describe block replaced by a comment explaining the merge). No coverage loss. No finding.

=== 4. THE AC5 STRING REPLAY -- VERIFIED PLAUSIBLE AND CORRECTLY PROVENANCED ===
Read plugin_interface.ex:221-224 directly: `handle_yield_result(nil, task, handler, timeout_ms)` constructs exactly `"plugin handler #{inspect(handler)} did not respond within #{timeout_ms}ms"`. With handler = Letflow.Engine.Wasm.PluginHandler and timeout_ms = 200 (the call_timeout_test.exs replay's own captured invocation shape), this produces byte-for-byte `"plugin handler Letflow.Engine.Wasm.PluginHandler did not respond within 200ms"` -- exactly the captured_reason literal now in call_timeout_test.exs (:180-182). Real and plausible, not fabricated. The replay still proves what the original proved: CallTimeout.classify/1 is a pure function over a string, so a captured-string replay of the OUTER-timeout shape is exactly as rigorous a test of classify/1's own pattern-matching correctness as a fresh live dispatch -- this is the identical, already-established technique this same file already uses once (verified at call_timeout_test.exs:113-139, the pre-existing AC5-sibling capture, confirmed real). Provenance is commented at the call site (date 2026-09-05, exact invocation shape, live source named as plugin_handler_test.exs:152/AC5) -- correctly narrowed from the design's own S6.3.1 over-attribution (which named TWO live sources, :152 and :393; CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's regate-2 already caught that :393 never constructs this string at all, and the shipped test comment correctly cites only :152). No finding.

=== 5. THE DISPATCH COUNT -- MAJOR: the design's and the implementation handoff's '6' is only correct under one specific, unstated reading; taken at face value against the table's own rows, it is 7 ===
Counted every live wasmex/PluginInterface/PluginHandler call inside the five @tag :wasm_hang tests, directly from the shipped test files (not from the handoff's or design's own arithmetic): call_timeout_test.exs AC2 = 2 raw Wasmex.call_function/4 calls (lines 95 and 116, both on the SAME pid/Store); host_api_write_test.exs = 1 (line ~480); plugin_handler_test.exs AC5 = 1 (line 178), AC3 = 1 (line 424, via handle_node/1), AC4 = 2 (lines 507 and 513). Sum = 2+1+1+1+2 = 7 live invocation call sites, not 6 -- confirmed independently via `grep -n 'Wasmex.call_function\|PluginInterface.invoke\|PluginHandler.handle_node' ` restricted to these test bodies, and cross-checked against `grep -n 'try_acquire' test/letflow/engine/wasm/*.exs`, which correctly returns exactly 6 (matching the LEASE-acquisition count, not the native-dispatch count) -- AC2's second call deliberately does NOT acquire a second lease (design S6.2's own documented exception, correctly implemented).

The '6' becomes correct ONLY under a specific, load-bearing distinction the design states once (S0 item 1: 'the leak is one permanently-blocked Tokio task per Store, not per raw invocation') and then never re-applies explicitly to AC2's own row: AC2's second call reuses the SAME already-wedged pid/Store as its first call (confirmed at call_timeout_test.exs:91, one Wasmex.start_link/1 for both calls), so per the design's own S0 rule, that second call does NOT open a fresh Store and therefore does NOT leak a second, independent Tokio thread -- it queues behind the Store its first call already permanently wedged. Under THAT reading, AC2 contributes exactly 1 net leaked pool slot, and the true total is 1(AC2)+1(host_api)+1(AC5)+1(AC3)+2(AC4) = 6, matching the claimed number and making OQ-E's arithmetic (6 leaked slots vs. a measured 4-slot pool) internally consistent.

This reading is very likely what the design intends -- S6.1's own table row for AC2 says '2 (the test's own second call on the now-wedged pid is itself a second live hang, per S1.2's Store-stays-wedged finding)', which is consistent with treating it as a second HANG event but not a second independent LEAK event once S0's per-Store rule is applied. But the design and the ELIXIR-DEV handoff both state '6 hang dispatches' as a flat count without ever performing or citing this Store-level reconciliation explicitly -- S6.1's table literally sums to 7 if 'dispatch' means 'call site' (which is how S6.2's own prose otherwise uses the word, e.g. 'each call is an independent admission event' for AC4's two calls), and nowhere does the document state 'AC2's 2 dispatches count as only 1 net pool-slot-leak for the purposes of the >6 threshold.' This is exactly the kind of internal-consistency question this project's audit-trail discipline (see docs/anti-patterns.md's 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source') exists to catch before a load-bearing number gets inherited uncorrected -- OQ-E's own '>6' threshold, and S10's post-hoc argument about whether the strict model 'holds,' both depend on knowing precisely what is being counted, and as written a careful future reader (or TEST-RUNNER measuring post-merge CI) cannot tell from the document alone whether the number to compare against the measured pool size is 6 (net Store-leaks) or 7 (call sites) without independently re-deriving the Store-reuse argument, which no location in the design states outright. Raised to MAJOR rather than MINOR because this is not a wording nit on a settled number -- it is genuine ambiguity in the one number the whole OQ-E gate and S10's ORCH decision are computed against, and the two plausible readings disagree by an amount that matters at N=4.

Recommendation, not itself a merge blocker: add one explicit sentence to design S6.1 (or S6.3.1) stating the Store-level reconciliation ('AC2's 2 dispatches share one Store and therefore count as 1 net pool-slot-leak, not 2, under S0 item 1's own rule -- so the true leaked-slot total feeding OQ-E's threshold is 6, distinct from the 7 raw call sites') so a future reader (including whoever performs the post-merge CI observation S10's falsifiable prediction calls for) is comparing the right number. File this as a docs-only follow-up; it does not require touching shipped code or tests.

=== 6. NON-VACUITY -- INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED ===
Ran test/letflow/engine/wasm/invocation_lease_test.exs myself (MIX_TEST_PARTITION=9, isolated from the shared wasm_hang subprocess and from concurrent sibling sessions observed on this host -- see note below): clean baseline `Result: 6 passed`. Applied ELIXIR-DEV's own MUTATION 1 (`if state.in_use < state.cap do` -> `if true do` in try_acquire's handle_call) and reran: `Result: 2/6 passed` (4 failed) -- matches ELIXIR-DEV's own reported '4 of 6 tests FAILED'. Reverted via the pre-mutation backup and reran: `Result: 6 passed` again, confirming the revert was clean and no state leaked. Did not additionally re-run MUTATION 2 (monitor-skip) myself -- accepted on ELIXIR-DEV's report given mutation 1 already independently confirms the harness discriminates real defects, and did not want to make a second speculative edit to shared test infrastructure while sibling sessions are active on this host. No finding; non-vacuity confirmed for at least one claimed mutation, directly reproduced, not merely trusted.

=== 7. CHALLENGE OF SS10's OQ-E RESOLUTION -- reasoning is defensible, not merge-past-red wearing better clothes, but its own argument is slightly overstated ===
This is NOT the ISS-0441 pattern. ISS-0441 warns against calling a red CI gate 'probably fine' without reading the log or without a causal argument -- i.e. asserting a conclusion the evidence does not support. What S10 does is the opposite motion: it takes the DESIGN's OWN predictive model (deterministic exhaustion once dispatches exceed the measured pool size) and tests that model against real CI outcomes across four actual runs at the PRE-change dispatch count of 8, finding the model's own strongest prediction (dispatches 5-8 fail on EVERY run) is falsified by real data (one run passed 7/7 outright). That is evidence-based model-checking, not schedule pressure dressed up as reasoning -- the artifact it produces (a narrowed claim, ISS-0418 kept open, a stated falsifiable prediction for post-merge observation) is exactly the shape core-directives.md's 'Failure Attribution Is Structural, Never By Count-Matching' section asks for: a demonstrated mechanism, evidenced by measurement, not asserted by feel.

However, the argument is more forceful than it needs to be and slightly overclaims in one place: S10 says 'a threshold inherited from a model whose predictions are contradicted by measurement cannot itself gate a decision.' That is too strong. Falsifying the model's DETERMINISTIC/worst-case form (100% failure past N=pool-size) does not establish that the '>6' threshold itself is wrong -- it is equally consistent with a PROBABILISTIC model (each additional leaked slot past some safety margin raises failure PROBABILITY, not certainty) under which the '>6' threshold would still be directionally correct, just not deterministic -- which is actually what the pre-change baseline data (7/7, 6/7, 5/7, 5/7 -- a non-trivial but non-100% failure rate) looks like. S10's own falsifiable prediction at the end ('the subprocess should now fail materially LESS often... if not, the diagnosis itself needs re-diagnosis') is the right response to THIS weaker, more defensible framing, and is stated correctly -- but the paragraph immediately preceding it oversells the case as 'the threshold cannot gate the decision' when the more honest statement is 'the threshold's DETERMINISTIC justification is falsified; whether a weaker probabilistic version of the same threshold still held was never separately checked, so shipping is a bet made explicit, not a proven-safe threshold override.' The practical outcome (ship, narrow the claim, keep the issue open, commit to a falsifiable check) is the same either way, and every constraint that actually matters (production stays uncapped; ISS-0418 stays open; no closure claimed) is honored -- so this is recorded as MINOR (an argument-precision issue in S10's own prose), not grounds to reject the decision. ORCH did not use this reasoning to quietly satisfy a gate by editing what it measures (core-directives.md's own forbidden move) -- the measurement result (N=4) is reported accurately and unmasked, and the gate's CONSEQUENCE (an unqualified 'fixes the flake' claim) is correctly withheld. This is a defensible engineering call, recorded as such, with one prose-precision MINOR.

=== 8. SCOPE -- CONFIRMED, byte-for-byte ===
`git diff main...HEAD --stat -- lib/letflow/engine/plugin_interface.ex lib/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler.ex lib/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout.ex` returns EMPTY -- all three files are untouched by this branch, confirming S1/S8.1's scope boundary held in the actual implementation, not merely in the handoff's claim. The only lib/ changes are the new invocation_lease.ex and the additive infrastructure.ex supervision wiring; the only test/ changes are the three files named in S6/S11 plus the new invocation_lease_test.exs. No scope creep: no new behaviour abstraction was introduced ahead of what ISS-0418 needs (the module is a plain counting semaphore, not a generic framework), and the design's own S3 argues explicitly, and correctly, why this is NOT built as an extension of Letflow.Admission -- reusing Admission's shape as precedent rather than its code is the right call given Admission's own documented non-monitoring crash semantics (verified at admission.ex, matches the design's characterization). No finding.

=== VERIFICATION ENVIRONMENT NOTE ===
Several erl.exe processes (10 total, all started within the same ~5-minute window as this review, per `Get-Process erl | Select StartTime`) were observed active on this host during review -- assessed as a live sibling session's own test run, not stale orphans from a crashed prior run (all near-simultaneous start times, none idle/long-running), so they were NOT killed, per this host's known concurrent-sibling-session pattern. Verification above was scoped to avoid contending with them: compile/format checks (isolated, no DB), the new invocation_lease_test.exs run under MIX_TEST_PARTITION=9 (isolated DB partition), and static diff/grep verification for everything else. Did not run the shared mix test --only wasm_hang subprocess myself, since that is exactly the contended, small-pool resource this whole issue is about and doing so here would not produce a meaningful measurement anyway (this dev host's own schedulers_online()=16 diverges from the CI target already, per the design's own S5.5/S6.3.1 discussion) -- OQ-E's own required measurement is CI-only by the design's own text, not reproducible meaningfully on a dev host, so this is not a gap in this review.

issues.finding: The design's and ELIXIR-DEV's implementation handoff's claimed '6 hang dispatches' (the number OQ-E's '>6' threshold and S10's ORCH decision are computed against) is only correct under an unstated Store-level reconciliation: AC2's 2 raw Wasmex.call_function/4 calls (call_timeout_test.exs:95,116) both target the SAME pid/Store (Wasmex.start_link/1 called once, at line 91), so per the design's own S0 item 1 rule ('the leak is one permanently-blocked Tokio task per Store, not per raw invocation'), AC2's second call does not open a fresh Store and therefore does not leak a second, independent Tokio thread -- it queues behind the Store its first call already wedged. Counted as raw call sites (which is how S6.2's own prose elsewhere uses 'dispatch', e.g. calling AC4's two independent calls 'an independent admission event' each), the real total across the five @tag :wasm_hang tests is 7, not 6 (AC2=2, host_api=1, AC5=1, AC3=1, AC4=2). No location in the design states the Store-level reconciliation explicitly, so a future reader (including whoever performs S10's own called-for post-merge CI observation) cannot tell from the document alone whether the number to compare against a measured pool size is 6 (net Store-leaks) or 7 (call sites). Does not block this PASS because the underlying reasoning that makes '6' the operative number for pool-exhaustion purposes is sound once reconstructed and no test coverage is actually missing -- but the ambiguity sits directly on the one number this run's central escalation (OQ-E) and ORCH's own S10 argument depend on, which is exactly the class of inherited-uncorrected-number risk this project's anti-patterns doc already warns about. Fix: add one explicit sentence to S6.1 or S6.3.1 stating the Store-level reconciliation and the resulting 6-vs-7 distinction, as a docs-only follow-up.

issues.location: lib/letflow/design/iss0418-wasm-concurrency-cap.md S10 (OQ-E RESOLUTION), paragraph beginning 'What this means for the ">6" threshold specifically'
issues.finding: S10 argues 'a threshold inherited from a model whose predictions are contradicted by measurement cannot itself gate a decision,' but the four cited CI runs (7/7, 6/7, 5/7, 5/7 at the pre-change dispatch count of 8) only falsify the model's DETERMINISTIC/worst-case form (100% failure once dispatches exceed the measured pool size) -- they are equally consistent with a PROBABILISTIC model under which the '>6' threshold remains directionally meaningful even though not deterministic. The practical decision (ship, narrow the claim, keep ISS-0418 open, record a falsifiable prediction) is unaffected and is the right call either way, and S10's own closing falsifiable-prediction paragraph is already framed correctly for the weaker, more defensible version of this argument -- but the preceding paragraph overstates what the four data points actually prove. Not blocking; a prose-precision fix to S10's own reasoning, at ORCH's discretion given this design's rework budget is exhausted.

Carried forward, unchanged, from all three prior gates (already recorded in step-02b-code-design-validator-regate2.json): the original S8 code-shape sketch proposing try_acquire/release inside handle_node/1 remains present verbatim in the document, marked superseded by S8.1 rather than removed. Still not blocking -- clearly flagged as superseded -- recorded again per this project's audit-trail discipline.

Confirmed the file's own docstring is accurate ('does NOT prove the lease's PLACEMENT is correct against a real hang') -- not a defect, recorded only because it is exactly the kind of honest self-scoping this project's audit discipline rewards and a future reader benefits from seeing it re-affirmed independently rather than only self-asserted. No action needed.

next_action: PASS. Route to TEST-DESIGNER per WF-03's normal Step 2d->3 sequencing (this run's own step numbering already used 'Step 3' for ELIXIR-DEV, so the next producing step is TEST-DESIGNER's own coverage-adequacy pass over the already-shipped tests, per the standard pipeline shape) or, if ORCH judges the existing TEST-DESIGNER-equivalent coverage in this run (test/letflow/engine/wasm/invocation_lease_test.exs, already written by ELIXIR-DEV per design S6.5's own instruction) sufficient, proceed directly to TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 real-CI verification -- which is now the step that must carry out S6.3.1's own 'required verification' obligation for any FUTURE re-measurement (already discharged once for this run via the three CI runs ELIXIR-DEV and ORCH already cited) and, per S10's own falsifiable prediction, must record the post-merge wasm_hang failure rate for comparison against the pre-change baseline (3 failures in 6 attempts). Also route the MAJOR finding (dispatch-count ambiguity) to whoever next touches this design doc as a docs-only follow-up -- it does not block this gate or require new code/test changes.
